# Shape atlas S1 — what kinds of path do momentum events make? — STOP (section 8) for Cooper to read the atlas

*exploratory, hindsight used by design; nothing here is a tested result.*

## 1. Coverage and assertions

15,519 events with τ (all of D1 with τ). One tick pass, 904 s.

| view | available | not available (reasons) |
|---|---|---|
| post-τ, N = 50 | 15,515; own null computed on 15,513 | 4 |
| post-τ, N = 100 | 15,515; own null computed on 15,513 | 4 |
| post-τ, N = 200 | 15,515; own null computed on 15,513 | 4 |
| run-up (N = 100) | 14,409 (thin, < 250 prints: 4,361) | {'no_print_before_tau': 909, 'tau_in_auction_minute': 185, 'sigma_zero': 16} |
| whole day (N = 100) | 15,519 | none |

| assertion (a failure is a stop) | result |
|---|---|
| bucket volume conservation in every view | instruments.bucketize asserts on every view and rung; none raised; max bucket-volume relative error post100 1.9e-14, runup 1.9e-14, whole_day 1.9e-14 |
| every resampled path has exactly G points | asserted in s1common.resample (G = 100) on every path |
| `tau_ns` int64 | True |
| null paths go through the identical code path (identity index, no demeaning, output identical) | True |
| null draws are row-stable (the first r of 200 = a request for r) | True |
| post-τ components equal b2's (b2 - s1 / max(1, b2) <= 1e-9) | True (max 8.1e-12) |

## 2. Theory types (section 3) — real share vs the share noise alone produces

Rules declared before the run, first match wins, on each event's own null percentiles: **runaway** rise_pct >= 90 and u_peak >= 0.9; **burst** rise_pct >= 90 and u_peak < 0.5; **slow_climb** rise_pct >= 90 and 0.5 <= u_peak < 0.9; **exhausted** u_peak < 0.05 and rise_pct < 50; **fade** fall_pct >= 90 (and none of the above); **chop** everything else.
